research.title: Logic gate
research.note: The About page facts on what a gate is and why NAND alone is enough: the seven starting chips are exactly these gates, and every one of The Sixteen two-input functions can be built from NAND chips in the sandbox.

research.title: Claude Shannon
research.note: Supplies the About page fact "Switches that do algebra": Every level is that idea: a truth table on one side, switches and lamps on the other, and a circuit that makes them agree.

research.title: Flip-flop (electronics)
research.note: Supplies the About page fact "Memory from a loop": Latch Up is exactly this loop. Edge Catcher builds the clock-edge version from two latches.

research.title: Adder (electronics)
research.note: Supplies the About page fact "Adding in columns": The Adders chapter is this ladder: half adder, full adder, then four columns in a row.

research.title: Apollo Guidance Computer
research.note: Supplies the About page fact "A real computer made of NOR gates": Your tiny computer has four-bit words and four instructions, but it is the same kind of machine: gates, remembered bits, and a counter.

other.title: Pyodide
other.note: Runs the game's Python rules in the browser through WebAssembly (version 0.26.4, loaded from a CDN), so the game needs no server of its own and no build step.

other.title: Generated sound (Web Audio)
other.note: The optional clicks, tone and bell are generated in code with the browser's Web Audio API, from plain sine tones; there are no audio files and nothing is downloaded.
